title: Data Abstraction
subtitle: Rational numbers, geometry and procedural pairs behind tested interfaces
description: Follow SICP’s rational-number, point and segment, procedural-pair and interval examples in Python. Specify constructor-selector laws, keep clients independent of storage, count where normalization work happens, and see why interval formulas that are algebraically equal give different bounds.
estimateNote: Author estimate, not measured on learners: lesson about 20–25 minutes (2,400 words, seven code blocks); lab about 12 + 12 + 6 + 10 + 20 = 60 minutes. The book's own text is a reference and is not counted.
sourceAttribution: Based on SICP §§2.1.1–2.1.4 by Harold Abelson and Gerald Jay Sussman with Julie Sussman. Rational numbers, segments, procedural pairs and intervals are the book’s examples translated to Python; the lab uses exercises 2.1, 2.3 and 2.4 and the parallel-resistor formulas of exercises 2.13–2.16.
